Logan City, January 2, 1861.

I will give a little of our history from the old country up to the present, as correctly as my memory allows. We left Bethania, Ffestiniog, on April 14, 1856, and reached Liverpool. We reached the American continent on May 24, [unclear in Welsh] Boston. After a day or two we took the railroad to Iowa City, where we remained for nearly three weeks. From there we began our journey across the plains with handcarts to Utah.

We stayed for a few days in Salt Lake City after arriving on October 2. The journey was very hard because we did not have half enough food, and pulling the handcart was hard. After several days my father and the [unclear in Welsh] went to Farmington, eighteen miles north of Salt Lake City. I then went twenty-two miles farther to Ogden with Erastus Bingham and remained there for four [unclear in Welsh], after which I returned to my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters.

Logan City, July 12, 1870

On June 1, 1870, I set out for Smithfield to fetch Hannah Roberts and returned to Logan. The next day I set out for Salt Lake City and arrived there on the fourth. On the sixth we went to the House of the Lord to be united for time and eternity by Joseph F. Smith, one of the Apostles and a son of Hyrum Smith the patriarch. Hugh and Mary Roberts are Hannah's parents. At present they live in Smithfield, Cache County, Utah Territory. They emigrated from Eglwys bach, Pembrokeshire, Wales, to Salt Lake City in the year 1864.

Robert David Roberts

Hannah Roberts was born March 27, 1847, at Eglwys bach, Pembrokeshire.

R. D. Roberts

January 4, 1871

Ann, our sister, gave birth to a fine son at six [unclear in Welsh: in the morning], weighing ten pounds. His name was David Roberts Hopkin. He was blessed by [unclear: Benjamin M. Munnon] on May 4, 1871.

March 22, 1871

Elizabeth, our sister, gave birth to twin girls on February 8, 1871, at Farmington, Utah, Davis County. Their names were Ann and Margaret. Ann was born at forty minutes past nine in the evening (9:40); Margaret at thirty minutes past ten (10:30). Ann weighed five and three-quarter pounds (5 3/4 lbs); Margaret five and one-quarter pounds (5 1/4 lbs). [Sentence continues on PDF page 85]

April 9, 1875

February 21. Daniel Roberts, my brother, was rebaptized by Robert Davidson; he was confirmed by Thomas McNeil, senior.

March 27. Daniel set out for Salt Lake City to marry and met his beloved at Hamilton Station. Taliesin, her brother, came with her from Samaria, Oneida County, Idaho. July 4, 1875

Today I was baptized into the United Order by Robert Davidson; I was confirmed by Thomas McNeil.

On the tenth, Hannah Roberts, my wife, was baptized by Joseph White; she was confirmed by Robert Davidson.

October 4, 1875

Today mother and Ann Hopkin, my sister, were baptized into the United Order by Joseph White. Ann was confirmed by Henry Ballard, and mother by Charles C. Card.

October 16, 1875

On the eighth, Ann Hopkin, my sister, set out for Salt Lake City. On the ninth mother and I set out, and we arrived there on the tenth. We attended conference meetings. On the eleventh I received my citizenship paper. On the thirteenth we were baptized in the House of the Lord for a number of relatives. We do not know who confirmed us. Wrth edrych ar ei phriod a'i phlant bach, y ty a'r amgylchoedd lle yr oedd wedi bod yn rhodio ac yn amcanu i wneuthur ei hun a'i phriod a'i phlant yn gyffurus, ei mynwes yn oer, y tafod yn fud a'r wefusau yn nghlo, y wedd a'r olwg wedi pellhau, yr yspryd wedi cyfodi ffo ymaith, a dim ond rhyw bridd gwael ac oer oedd i edrych arno, ac yn amser ei roi i orwedd cyn iddo falurio. Am ddau o'r gloch cludwyd ei gweddillion i'r old Hall, lle y cawsom bregeth dda yn Gymraeg gan Owen Thomas, a'r olwg ddiweddaf ar ei gweddillion. Hi a roddodd enedigaeth i saith o blant, tri o fechgyn a phedair o ferched; mae pedwar yn fyw yn bresennol, dau fachgen a dwy ferch. Ar yr ugeinfed (20) cychwynasom dros adref; [unclear: ar un dydd cyrhaeddasom trwy storm i fachgen Conar i dori ei fraich] ychydig uwchlaw ei benelin. Ar yr un dydd, sef 16, a daeth ein chwaer Elizabeth i ymadael a'r fuchedd hon. Mae yn gwella yn dda. Hwn wedi ei ysgrifenu ar y Mehefin 3, 1877.

Medi 4, 1877

Taliesin Hughes a'i chwaer Maria Roberts, a'r eneth ieuanc Elizabeth ein chwaer, a merch ifanc o'r enw Jane Mason, tua deunaw mlwydd ei hoed, a briodwyd hwy gan William B. Preston yn ei dy. Dychwelodd a chyrhaeddasant hyd mor bell a Hamilton Station i dy Ann ein chwaer, lle yr oedd Jane ein chwaer.
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 90]

of severe cold and wind, and we were unable to go any farther than Square Town that day. On the eighteenth the weather was rather unpleasant, and we reached Samaria a few minutes after ten. Looking at her husband and her little children, the house and surroundings where she had moved about and sought to make herself, her husband, and her children comfortable, her breast was cold, her tongue silent and her lips closed, her appearance and expression gone, the spirit having risen and fled away, leaving only poor, cold earth to look upon, and it was time to lay it to rest before it crumbled. At about two o'clock her remains were carried to the old Hall, where we heard a good sermon in Welsh by Owen Thomas and took our last look at her remains. She gave birth to seven children, three boys and four girls; four are now living, two boys and two girls. On the twentieth we set out for home. [Uncertain Welsh wording concerning the return journey and Conar's boy breaking his arm a little above the elbow.] On that same day, the sixteenth, our sister Elizabeth departed this life. The boy is recovering well. This was written on June 3, 1877.

September 4, 1877

Taliesin Hughes and his sister Maria Roberts, with the young daughter of our sister Elizabeth, and a young woman named Jane Mason, about eighteen years old, were married by William B. Preston in his house. They returned as far as Hamilton Station, to the house of Ann, our sister, where Jane, our sister, was staying.

journalPages.welshTranscription:
Ebrill 10, 1878

Ymadawodd fy anwyl wraig a'r fuchedd hon yn dawel fel i gysgu. Cafodd afiechyd a phoen anghyffredin er dechreu Mawrth, efo'i dannedd i ddechreu; chwyddodd ei chorff yn debyg i'r dropsi. Roedd rhai o'r meddygon yn ei galw yn lled salach ac iawn. Ni chafodd fawr o iechyd ar ol briodi; ymsgariodd a'i [unclear: bron] yn agos i colli ei bywyd pob dro. Mi roedd yn edrych ac yn deimlo yn well y gaeaf hwn nag y bu ers llawer dydd; er hyn i gyd ymaflodd y dinistrwr yn ei chyfansoddiad a gwahanodd yr ysbryd a'r corff. Mi roedd yn wraig ardderchog o lan yn fan a chefnil ac yn medru ei gwaith yn eitha iawn; yn fam rhagorol iawn i'w phlant bach, yn eu dysgu i weddio ac i gydnabod Duw mor fuan ac y byddent yn bosibl; mi roedd yn gymydog cariadus a heddychlon. Ar y deuddegfed (12), am unarddeg o'r gloch (11) y bore, aethom a'i gweddillion i'r hen Hall, lle y cawsom gyfarfod da: gweddi gan Thomas McNeil; pregethau gan John Parry, Robert Davidson a Henry Ballard; diweddiad gan David W. Davies; arweiniwyd y canu gan Alizander Lewis. Claddwyd hi yn mynwent Logan; gweddiwyd gan Benjamin Williams yn y fynwent. Hwn wedi ei ysgrifenu ar y 5ed Mai.

Chwefror 21, 1878

Sarah Ann, gwraig Daniel ein brawd, a rodd enedigaeth i eneth fach am haner awr wedi chwech yn yr hwyr. Mehefin 6 bendithiwyd hi gan Thomas McNeil; ei henw yw Margaret Roberts. Mae yn edrych yn faban clws ac y cyfyd ferch lan [continues on PDF page 93]
journalPages.translation:
April 10, 1878

My beloved wife departed this life peacefully, as though falling asleep. She had suffered unusual illness and pain since the beginning of March, beginning with her teeth; her body swelled as in dropsy. [Some medical wording remains uncertain.] She had little health after marrying and twice miscarried, coming close to losing her life each time. She had looked and felt better this winter than for many days, yet despite everything the destroyer took hold of her constitution and separated spirit from body. She was an excellent, clean, and thrifty wife who managed her work very well; an excellent mother to her little children, teaching them to pray and acknowledge God as soon as they were able; and a loving, peaceable neighbor. On the twelfth, at eleven in the morning, we took her remains to the old Hall, where we had a good meeting: prayer by Thomas McNeil; sermons by John Parry, Robert Davidson, and Henry Ballard; benediction by David W. Davies; singing led by Alizander Lewis. She was buried in the Logan cemetery, where Benjamin Williams offered prayer. This was written on May 5.

February 21, 1878

Sarah Ann, the wife of our brother Daniel, gave birth to a little girl at half past six in the evening. On June 6 she was blessed by Thomas McNeil; her name is Margaret Roberts. She appears to be a pretty baby who will grow into a beautiful girl [continues on PDF page 93]
journalPages.notes:
- The April 1878 obituary and funeral entry has a confirmed close-paraphrase parallel on RDR PDF page 19. RDR expands and smooths several medical and character descriptions; uncertain Welsh medical wording remains cautious here.
- Welsh source forms `Robert Davidson` and `Alizander Lewis` are preserved despite RDR's normalized `Robert Davieson` and `Alexander Lewis`.
- The February 1878 birth entry is nonchronological and continues onto page 93. It has a confirmed close parallel on RDR PDF page 19.
- First-person spousal language and handwriting continuity support confirmed attribution to Robert D. Roberts as content author and scribe, although no signature appears on this page.

Rhagfyr 29, 1878

Jane ein chwaer, gwraig Conar Hughes, yn byw yn Samaria, a rhodd enedigaeth i fachgan yn edrych yn dda ac yn gryf am bum munud i wyth yn y bore. Ei enw yw Conar Hughes.

Ebrill 3, 1879

Bedyddiwyd David Robert Roberts gan William Waterson; cadarnhawyd ef gan Robert Davidson yr un dydd. Ac hefyd bedyddiwyd David Roberts Hopkin gan Christian L. Larson, a chadarnhawyd ef gan Henry Ballard yr un dydd.

Mai 26, 1879

Am ddeg munud wedi saith yn y bore (10 wedi 7), Ann Hopkin ein chwaer a rodd enedigaeth i fachgen cryf a bywiog yn pwyso deg pwys (10 lbs). Bendithiwyd ef gan Christian L. Larson Gorffenaf 3, 1879; ei enw William John Hopkin.

Mehefin 23, 1879

Am ychydig o funudau i un o'r gloch y prydnawn bu i David Taliesin Hughes farw o glefyd y gwddf ar ol ychydig o dri diwrnod. Aeth yn sal yn yr ysgol fore Gwener a bu farw.

Hyrum Hughes a clafychodd o'r un clefyd ar yr unfed ar hugain (21) o'r un mis [continues on PDF page 94]
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 92]

December 29, 1878

Jane, our sister and the wife of Conar Hughes, living in Samaria, gave birth to a boy who looked well and strong at five minutes to eight in the morning. His name is Conar Hughes.

April 3, 1879

David Robert Roberts was baptized by William Waterson and confirmed by Robert Davidson that same day. David Roberts Hopkin was also baptized by Christian L. Larson and confirmed by Henry Ballard that same day.

May 26, 1879

At ten minutes past seven in the morning, Ann Hopkin, our sister, gave birth to a strong and lively boy weighing ten pounds. He was blessed by Christian L. Larson on July 3, 1879; his name is William John Hopkin.

June 23, 1879

A few minutes before one in the afternoon, David Taliesin Hughes died of a throat disease after an illness of about three days. He became ill at school on Friday morning and died.

Hyrum Hughes became ill with the same disease on the twenty-first of the same month [continues on PDF page 94]

ac a fu farw am ddau o'r gloch y bore 25. Mi roedd ef clu yn glefyd. Wedi ei eni Mawrth 6, 1874, mae'r ddau yn fechgyn braf iawn ac yn ymddangos y buasent yn tyfu i fechgyn cryf. Claddwyd hwy yn Samaria, Oneida, Tiriogaeth Idaho, lle y mae eu tad yn byw.

Logan City, Hydref 4, 1879

Sarah Ann Roberts, gwraig Daniel Roberts, a rhodd enedigaeth i ferch fechan yn yr hwyr am un o'r gloch y prydnawn, yn pwyso 9 lbs. Rhagfyr 4 bendithiwyd hi gan Thomas McNeil; ei henw yw Ida Roberts.

Awst 5, 1880

Sarah Ann, gwraig Daniel Roberts, a fedyddiwyd ar unwaith gan Christian L. Larson. Cadarnhawyd hi gan Henry Ballard.

Chwefror 19, 1881

Thomas J. Roberts a ail fedyddiwyd gan Henry Ballard; cadarnhawyd ef gan yr un. Ac ar y 24ain, fe a'i amcanwraig Margaret Davies a aethant i Dy yr Arglwydd yn Ninas y Llyn Halen, a unwyd yn nghwlwm y cyfamod tragwyddol i fod yn wr a gwraig am amser ac am dragwyddoldeb gan Daniel H. Wells.

Margaret yn cael ei hindowment ar yr un pryd [continues on PDF page 95]
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 93]

and died at about two o'clock in the morning on the twenty-fifth. He had been very ill with the disease. Born on March 6, 1874, the two were fine boys who appeared likely to grow into strong young men. They were buried in Samaria, Oneida County, Idaho Territory, where their father lives.

Logan City, October 4, 1879

Sarah Ann Roberts, the wife of Daniel Roberts, gave birth to a little girl at about one o'clock in the afternoon, weighing nine pounds. On December 4 she was blessed by Thomas McNeil; her name is Ida Roberts.

August 5, 1880

Sarah Ann, the wife of Daniel Roberts, was rebaptized by Christian L. Larson. She was confirmed by Henry Ballard.

February 19, 1881

Thomas J. Roberts was rebaptized by Henry Ballard and confirmed by the same man. On the twenty-fourth, he and his intended wife, Margaret Davies, went to the House of the Lord in Salt Lake City and were united in the bond of the everlasting covenant as husband and wife for time and all eternity by Daniel H. Margaret received her endowment at the same time [continues on PDF page 95]

journalPages.welshTranscription:
[continuation from PDF page 94]

Miss Davies a aned yn Rhosllanerchrugog, Cymru, yn Sir Ddinbych, 30 Mehefin 1854.

Bedyddiwyd hi gan Henry Hatfield yn Liverpool. Cadarnhawyd gan Joseph H. Smith, Awst 1877.

Ymfudodd i Utah yn y flwyddyn 1878, a chyrhaeddodd Dinas y Llyn Halen ac arhosodd hi efo teulu Mr William Williams, Kensington, nes yr oedd yn Ebrill 1880, pan y daeth hi a'i chwaer Polly, yr hon a ymfudodd yn y flwyddyn 1879 i Ddinas y Llyn Halen, pan y daethant i Logan a rhentu lle bychan gan Mrs W. H. Garry, ac yr oedd yn cadw busnes gwnio lle y maent yn bresennol.

Ei rhieni yw Robert ac Ann Davies. Bedyddiwyd hwy yn Rhosllanerchrugog, Cymru, yn y flwyddyn 1855 gan John Berry, Elder. Yn Ebrill y flwyddyn 1858 daethant i fyw i Manchester.

Yn y flwyddyn 1860 daethant i fyw i Liverpool, ac ymfudasant o Liverpool i Utah Hydref 18, 1879, a chyrhaeddasant Utah, Logan, Tachwedd 10, 1879.

Mae dau fab a thair neu bedair o ferched yn y wlad eto heb ddod yma eto.
journalPages.translation:
[continuation from PDF page 94]

Miss Davies was born in Rhosllanerchrugog, Denbighshire, Wales, on June 30, 1854.

She was baptized by Henry Hatfield in Liverpool and confirmed by Joseph H. Smith in August 1877.

She emigrated to Utah in 1878 and arrived in Salt Lake City, where she stayed with the family of Mr. William Williams in Kensington until April 1880. Then she and her sister Polly, who had emigrated to Salt Lake City in 1879, came to Logan and rented a small place from Mrs. W. H. Garry, where they kept a sewing business and remain at present.

Her parents are Robert and Ann Davies. They were baptized in Rhosllanerchrugog, Wales, in 1855 by Elder John Berry. In April 1858 they moved to Manchester.

In 1860 they moved to Liverpool, and on October 18, 1879, they emigrated from Liverpool to Utah, arriving in Logan, Utah, on November 10, 1879.

Two sons and three or four daughters remain in the old country and have not yet come here.
journalPages.notes:
- This page completes the February 1881 Margaret Goodman Davies account begun on page 94. It has a confirmed close-paraphrase parallel on RDR PDF page 21.
- The Welsh preserves `Rhosllanerchrugog`, `Liverpool`, `Kensington`, and the family migration dates. RDR expands some English connective wording but follows the same sequence.
- The occupational phrase is translated cautiously as a sewing business; RDR specifies millinery. The Welsh wording should receive further specialist review before status promotion.
- No occurrence of `bach` or a distinct Robert-derived nickname is visible on pages 92–95.
- Handwriting continuity supports probable attribution to Robert D. Roberts as content author and scribe. No signature or secondary hand appears.
